title: ArtifactRef v1
description: An opaque HANDLE to binary content produced or consumed by a flow node — never the content itself, and never a path. Large binary data (an image, an audio file, a video) must not travel inside a flow's IR, node payloads, or run logs: it would bloat every persisted revision and run record, and would force every runtime to hold it in memory to pass it along. A node therefore emits a ref, and a downstream consumer resolves it through an authorizing endpoint. The `locality` field records WHERE the bytes actually are, which is what makes cross-device semantics honest: a desktop-local artifact is not silently uploaded to the cloud, and a consumer on another device is told so rather than handed a broken handle. Deliberately absent: any filesystem path, absolute URL, storage key, bucket name, or credential — everything here is safe to persist in a flow run log and to show a user.

$artifact.description: Opaque artifact id. Carries no meaning: not a path, not a hash, not derived from user input.

kind.description: Coarse content family. Matched against a port's `x-artifactKinds` at authoring time, so a node that accepts images cannot silently be wired an audio artifact.

mediaType.description: Exact IANA media type of the stored bytes.

byteSize.description: Size of the stored bytes. Present so a consumer can refuse before transferring.

digest.description: sha256 over the stored bytes. Lets a consumer verify what it received is what the producer wrote.

locality.description: Where the bytes live. `device` artifacts are never uploaded implicitly — a run on another device fails with a typed refusal instead of a silent transfer the user never approved.

deviceId.description: Required when locality is `device`; the only device that may read the bytes.

expiresAt.description: After this instant the ref resolves as expired, whether or not cleanup has run yet. Expiry is a property of the ref, not of the sweep schedule.

filename.description: Display name only. Never used to build a storage path.
